### Run FastMCP Server with HTTP Transport

Source: https://github.com/prefecthq/fastmcp/blob/main/docs/servers/server.mdx

This example shows how to configure and run the FastMCP server using the HTTP transport instead of the default STDIO. Specify the host and port for network accessibility.

```python
# Run with HTTP transport
mcp.run(transport="http", host="127.0.0.1", port=9000)
```

--------------------------------

### Configure FastMCP transport settings in run()

Source: https://github.com/prefecthq/fastmcp/blob/main/docs/getting-started/upgrading/from-fastmcp-2.mdx

FastMCP v3 moves transport and server settings from the `FastMCP()` constructor to the `run()` method. Pass host and port arguments when starting the server.

```python
# Before
mcp = FastMCP("server", host="0.0.0.0", port=8080)
mcp.run()
```

```python
# After
mcp = FastMCP("server")
mcp.run(transport="http", host="0.0.0.0", port=8080)
```

--------------------------------

### Run the Server

Source: https://github.com/prefecthq/fastmcp/blob/main/docs/getting-started/quickstart.mdx

Run the FastMCP server using its `run()` method with different transports.

```python
from fastmcp import FastMCP

mcp = FastMCP("My MCP Server")

@mcp.tool
def greet(name: str) -> str:
    return f"Hello, {name}!"

if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()
```

```python

    mcp.run(transport="http", port=8000)
```
